newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - Heartland Mid Cap rooted in value.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Heartland Mid Cap rooted in value.

text.p: The recently-launched Heartland Mid Cap Value Fund takes its name literally, according to Michael Berry, its portfolio manager.
"We want companies where the stock's busted," said Berry. "The fund is rooted in the value philosophy."

Among the gauges that Berry uses for the fund: low price-to-earnings ratios, low price-to-book ratios, and low price-to-cash flow ratios. Berry said he picks the measure depending on the industry, such as cash flow for broadcasting.
The fund, which began last month, also measures debt level and how much future cash flow will be used to pay down debt.
Berry also checks for "positive earnings dymamics," especially whether analysts are revising estimates up or down, and whether the company springs positive earnings surprises.

He studies management. "We want a pretty good management track record," he said. "We also like management that is respected in the industry." He feels safer if management owns a good block of the stock.
Another indicator is the technical chart on the stock.

Among top holdings are Agco Corp, which makes farm equipment and machinery; PHH Corp, which provides management and relocation services; and First Brands Corp, which makes consumer products such as Glad bags, kitty litter, and Simoniz polish. "They have top brands in several categories," he said of First Brands.
Other big holdings include Mid Ocean Ltd, a provider of property/catastrophe reinsurance; and Protective Life Corp, a life and health insurer.
Berry also likes "broken" technology shares, especially Advanced Micro Devices Inc, and National Semiconductor Corp, which makes semiconductor components for other products than personal computers.

Recent picks include Heilig-Meyers, a home furnishings retailer; and Signet Banking Corp, a $12 billion bank based in Virginia, Maryland, and Washington, D.C., in which the fund has been accumulating a position.
Berry's favorite industry sectors include financial services and manufacturing companies.
The fund will generally hold 45-50 stocks in the portfolio, and be almost fully invested, with a cash position as high as five percent.

Berry intends for the fund to be long-term investors. "Whether the aged bull is alive, dead or comatose, we do not advocate selling," Berry said in a report to investors. The philosophy is long-term investing, not market timing.
Berry expects the holding period for a stock to be about three years.
